posts.text:
More traffic hits your Kubernetes app. Do you add more Pods or make existing Pods bigger? 

This is the difference between HPA and VPA.

Both help manage resources in Kubernetes, but they solve different problems.

➡️ HPA — Horizontal Pod Autoscaler

Scales out by increasing the number of Pod replicas.

For example:
→ Traffic increases
→ CPU utilization rises
→ Kubernetes adds more Pods
→ Work gets distributed across more replicas

Best for stateless APIs, web applications, and workers that can handle additional replicas.

➡️ VPA — Vertical Pod Autoscaler

Scales up or down by adjusting the CPU and memory resources allocated to Pods.

Instead of adding replicas, it helps individual Pods get the resources they need.

But here's the catch.

VPA can disrupt workloads when resource changes require Pod recreation.

HPA can also struggle if the real bottleneck is a shared database rather than the application Pods.

And using HPA and VPA together requires care, especially when both react to CPU or memory utilization.

The goal isn't simply to scale.

It's to understand whether your application needs more instances or more resources per instance.

📌 05 November 2026

Team Leadership

- Lead and mentor junior and mid-level developers based in India.
- Manage hiring input, onboarding, performance and technical growth.
- Conduct code reviews, technical mentoring and pair programming.
- Establish engineering standards for testing, data validation, AI evaluation, observability and code quality.
- Standardize team practices for Claude Code and AI-assisted development.
- Lead sprint-level technical planning and resolve day-to-day engineering blockers.

Must-Have Technical Skills

- Python: Deep expertise with FastAPI, Flask or similar frameworks.
- Full Stack: React, Tailwind CSS and production application development.
- Databases: PostgreSQL, relational schema design, normalization and query optimization.
- AI / LLM: Claude, OpenAI or equivalent LLM APIs, prompt engineering, structured outputs and multimodal document processing.
- AI Development Tools: Strong practical proficiency with Claude Code or similar AI-assisted coding tools, agentic coding patterns and context management.
- Tool Calling: Function calling, tool schemas, argument validation, tool chaining and failure handling.
- Context Engineering: Token budgeting, context-window management, long-document processing and retrieval strategies.
- AI Security: Prompt injection awareness, adversarial inputs and untrusted-document safeguards.
- Automation: Background jobs, queues, retries, idempotency, workflow execution and monitoring.
- Cloud & DevOps: Azure preferred, containers, CI/CD, managed identities, object storage and secrets management.
- QA & AI Evaluation: Unit/integration testing, golden datasets, regression evaluations, validation frameworks and observability.
- Human-in-the-Loop: Review workflows, feedback loops, accuracy measurement and quality gates.
- Third-Party Integrations: OAuth, API security and credential management.

Preferred Qualifications

- LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, Temporal, Azure Durable Functions, Celery/RQ or similar frameworks.
- Model selection and cost optimization, prompt caching, batching and usage forecasting.
- Media, advertising or marketing technology experience.
- Unity Catalog, attribute-based access control and data governance.
- MCP servers and MCP-based developer workflows.
- DV360 SDF, The Trade Desk API or similar AdTech integrations.
- Data flywheel concepts, labeled datasets and AI feedback mechanisms.
- Open-source contributions or public AI/full-stack engineering projects.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are looking for a hands-on Engineering Lead / Architect who can independently design and build production-grade AI automation products while leading an engineering team.

The candidate must combine strong Python and full-stack engineering expertise with production LLM integration, system architecture, team leadership and delivery ownership.

Claude Fable just made “AI will replace junior developers” the loudest debate on my feed.

I’m a 2026 BCA grad who writes Java. Here’s my honest take from the other side of that debate:

I use Claude Code and Copilot while I build. They’re fast, but they don’t:

→ Decide how JWT + Spring Security roles map to real business rules
→ Take responsibility when the “working” endpoint breaks in production
→ Question the code they just wrote

What AI did change for me: less time on boilerplate, more time on design, validation and testing.

So when hiring a fresher in 2026, I’d skip asking “can you code?” and ask “can you explain every line the AI wrote?”

posts.text:
🚀 Containerizing a Full-Stack App with Docker | DevOps Internship Task

I recently completed a hands-on DevOps task where I took a full-stack Food Delivery application (React + Node.js + MongoDB) and containerized it from scratch.

🔧 What I built:
✅ Implemented the GitFlow branching strategy (main, dev, stg, feature) with Pull Requests
✅ Wrote Dockerfiles for the frontend (Vite) and backend (Express) using Node.js base images
✅ Ran MongoDB in a separate container with a persistent Docker volume
✅ Connected all services over a Docker network and orchestrated them with Docker Compose
✅ Deployed on AWS EC2 and configured Security Group rules to expose the application

⚠️ Challenges I faced:
• The frontend container kept crashing on startup. While debugging the build error, I found a suspicious, extremely long line in a config file that didn't belong there. I preserved it as evidence, replaced it with a clean config, and reported it to the team. It was a good reminder to always review third-party code before running it.
• The backend couldn't reach MongoDB using "localhost" inside the container. Fixed it by using the container name as the host on a shared network.
• Learned the importance of keeping secrets in .env files and rotating credentials when they are exposed.
💡 Key takeaways:
• Analyze the project (ports, env variables, start commands) before writing a Dockerfile
• Docker networks and volumes are essential for connected, stateful services
• Read the logs first. They usually tell you exactly what is wrong
• Never run untrusted code blindly

In this role:  You will be responsible for receiving blood specimens, performing blood tests, and studying the morphology of the components of blood. You will be responsible for maintaining and using various equipment in the Laboratory including automated, chemistry analyzers, ion-specific electrodes, osmometers, and other analyzers.  You will perform antibody screening, antibody identification, and cross-matching procedures required in the administration of blood/blood components and identify antibodies in donors or patients blood that could react adversely during transfusion.  You will notify nursing units and/or physicians of critical lab values.  You will implement new testing methods, products, and instrumentation as appropriate to keep department current with technology. Qualifications:  Graduate of an accredited Medical Technology program

Introduction At IBM Software, we transform client challenges into solutions. Building the worlds leading AI-powered, cloud-native products that shape the future of business and society. Youll work with diverse technologies, partners, and industries to design, develop, and deliver solutions that power digital transformation. With a culture that values innovation, growth, and continuous learning, IBM Software places you at the heart of IBMs product and technology landscape. Here, youll have the tools and opportunities to advance your career while creating software that changes the world. Your Role and Responsibilities Were not just building better tech. Were rewriting how data moves and what the world can do with it. With Confluent, data doesnt sit still. Our platform puts information in motion, streaming in near real-time so companies can react faster, build smarter, and deliver experiences as dynamic as the world around them. It takes a certain kind of person to join this team. Those who ask hard questions, give honest feedback, and show up for each other. No egos, no solo acts. Just smart, curious humans pushing toward something bigger, together. Senior Software Engineers II at Confluent take ownership of critical backend systems that underpin our data streaming platform. Youll lead the design and delivery of large-scale, distributed services that must be secure, highly available, and easy to operate across regions and clouds. The team owns a highly available, scalable metadata store - the source of truth that services across Confluent Cloud build on. It serves low-latency read and write APIs, and streams data in real time. The platform is a foundational backbone of a broader effort to re-architect Confluent Cloud and replacing bespoke, per-team datastores with a single self-serve platform. Daarna sta je klaar om klanten te ontvangen in de showroom en help je hen stap voor stap bij het samenstellen van hun ideale badkamer. Je luistert goed naar hun wensen, denkt mee in mogelijkheden en vertaalt dat naar een mooi en praktisch ontwerp. Naast het klantcontact maak je ook 3D-ontwerpen en stel je offertes op. Je zorgt ervoor dat de showroom er verzorgd uitziet en helpt af en toe bij het monteren van nieuwe producten in de showroom. Heb je nog geen ervaring in sanitair? Geen zorgen! In je eerste maanden leer je alles over badkamers, tegels en producten zodat jij klanten zelfverzekerd kunt adviseren. Wat wij bieden: Als Verkoopadviseur sanitair in Eindhoven krijg jij de volgende voordelen:Een salaris van € 2700 ,- tot € 3500 ,- op basis van jouw ervaring en jaarlijkse bonussen op basis van teamprestaties;Een uitdagende en afwisselende functie met klantcontact waarin je jezelf verder kan ontwikkelen;Een prettige werkomgeving;Leuke borrels, evenementen en uitjes met het gehele team;Een informele, no-nonsense en open bedrijfscultuur. Over het bedrijf: Je komt te werken bij een snelgroeiende badkamerspecialist met zowel een webshop als meerdere showrooms in Nederland, België en Duitsland. Je werkt in een betrokken en enthousiast team, waar aandacht voor de klant, deskundig advies en een goede sfeer centraal staan. Bedrijfsbreed ligt de gemiddelde leeftijd rond de 30 jaar en elk kwartaal worden er gezellige evenementen georganiseerd op het hoofdkantoor in Rosmalen, een leuke manier om collegas van andere vestigingen te leren kennen en successen samen te vieren! Vereisten: Je hebt minimaal MBO4 werk- en denkniveau;Je hebt een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal;Je bent commercieel sterk;Je bent loyaal, eerlijk en weet wat goede klantenservice betekent;Je vindt het niet erg af en toe in de weekenden te helpen.

🚀 Git Commands Cheatsheet Every Developer & Tester Should Know!

Working with Git becomes much easier when you know the right commands! 💻

Whether you're a beginner in software testing, a QA engineer, an automation tester, or a developer, these essential Git commands can help you manage your code efficiently. 👇

🔹 "git init" – Initialize a repository
🔹 "git status" – Check file changes
🔹 "git add" – Stage changes
🔹 "git commit" – Save changes to the repository
🔹 "git log" – View commit history
🔹 "git checkout" – Switch branches
🔹 "git branch" – Manage branches
🔹 "git fetch" – Retrieve updates from a remote repository
🔹 "git pull" – Fetch and integrate remote changes
🔹 "git push" – Upload commits to a remote repository
🔹 "git merge" – Combine branch changes
🔹 "git rebase" – Reapply commits onto another branch

🎯 Why should you learn Git?
✅ Track code changes
✅ Collaborate effectively with your team
✅ Manage branches and resolve conflicts
✅ Maintain a smooth development and testing workflow

posts.text:
Keyword matching is not about stuffing jargon.

It is about aligning your resume with the language the employer already used in the job description.

When an ATS scans your file, it looks for skills and titles that appear in that posting. If your resume says "team lead" and the role says "project manager," you can lose points even if the work is similar.

A simple habit helps:

1. Copy the job description
2. Note the repeated skills and tools
3. Mirror those exact phrases where they are honest fits

Then check whether your file is still readable by an ATS.

Free check: https://atsresumeos.com

#JobSearch #ATS #ResumeTips #CareerAdvice #Hiring

#hiring Zelfstandig werkend kok Cargill

Apply here: https://lnkd.in/gE6tsRvU

Kom jij ons helpen een prachtig menu samen te stellen bij Cargill op Schiphol? Als zelfstandig werkend kok zorg jij voor de lunchvoorbereidingen en denkt mee over de culinaire invulling van banqueting partijen. Good to know: je werkt tijdens kantoordagen en bent ieder weekend vrij!Jouw werkplekJe komt te werken in het bedrijfsrestaurant van Cargill Schiphol, die wereldwijd actief is in de voeding en landbouwproducten. Je werkt hier in een internationale kantooromgeving. Vermaat verzorgt hier de bedrijfshoreca voor de medewerkers en internationale collegas van Cargill. De locatie is goed bereikbaar met het ov, met station Schiphol op tien minuten loopafstand. Daarnaast is er gratis parkeergelegenheid. Het horecaconcept bestaat uit een restaurant met een vegetarisch en vegan aanbod en daarnaast een espressobar. Je komt te werken in een hecht team dat graag samenwerkt. Ook verzorgt Vermaat de banqueting voor interne bijeenkomsten. Dit maakt Cargill Schiphol een afwisselende en gezellige werkplek. Je bent beschikbaar op maandag t/m vrijdag en werkt tussen 7:00 uur en 19:00 uur. De exacte invulling van je rooster stemmen we af op de behoeften van de locatie en jouw beschikbaarheid.Jouw functieAls zelfstandig werkend kok bij Cargill, Schiphol laat jij iedere dag jouw vakmanschap zien in de keuken. Je werkt binnen een foodconcept waarbij je ruimte krijgt om jouw creativiteit en eigen stijl toe te voegen aan het aanbod. Met oog voor kwaliteit, smaak en presentatie zorg je ervoor dat gasten kunnen genieten van verrassende gerechten. Daarnaast houd je de keukenprocessen op orde en draag je bij aan een efficiënte en veilige werkomgeving.Als zelfstandig werkend kok:Bereid je dagelijks gerechten volgens het foodconcept en jouw eigen vakmanschap;Bewaak je de kwaliteit, presentatie en smaak van alle gerechten;Werk je zelfstandig en neem je verantwoordelijkheid binnen de keuken waar nodig;Zorg je ervoor dat HACCP-, arbo- en veiligheidsrichtlijnen worden nageleefd;Verzorg je, waar nodig, de bestellingen, houd je de allergenenregistraties bij en help je bij de keukenadministratie;Denk je mee over nieuwe recepten en weet je gasten steeds opnieuw te verrassen.Wat wij vragenWij zoeken een ervaren zelfstandig werkend kok met passie voor het vak. Je werkt nauwkeurig, houdt het hoofd koel tijdens drukke momenten en hebt oog voor kwaliteit. Met jouw ervaring en creativiteit lever je iedere dag een bijdrage aan een uitstekende culinaire beleving:Je hebt ervaring als zelfstandig werkend kok; Je werkt zowel zelfstandig als samen en neemt initiatief wanneer de situatie daarom vraagt;Je bent bekend met de HACCP-, arbo- en veiligheidsrichtlijnen;Je blijft ook tijdens piekmomenten efficiënt werken zonder concessies te doen aan kwaliteit;Jij weet gasten te verrassen met smaakvolle en gevarieerde gerechten;Je kunt op verzoek een Verklaring Omtrent het Ged

posts.text:
I’m not against it, but every platform has its own forte.

I recently noticed something. After getting home from work, I opened social media to relax and unwind, only to find myself scrolling through job vacancies.

It made me think about the purpose each platform serves.

When I open a hiring platform, I know exactly why I’m there. I’m looking for something that could give me purpose and stability. On social media, I find it hard to tell whether an opening is genuine, especially since so many people use it to promote their businesses. The motive isn’t always clear.

I do understand that it works well for creative roles. For content creators and digital marketers, social media is a way to showcase their work, and it’s often easier to reach them there than through a job platform.

However, I feel this applies to only about 20% of roles. For the remaining 80%, it doesn’t quite fit. Finding a developer through social media, for example, doesn’t sit right with me.

I’m not against the idea, but I believe that when a platform tries to serve both purposes, it slowly loses sight of what it was built for.

Do you see social media as a place to find a job or a place to switch off?

Share your thoughts in the comments. 👇

#Hiring #SocialMedia #JobSearch #FutureOfWork #RightPlatformRightPurpose #HiringTrends
